title: Why the band is called Jeter-Pillars
summary: The band was named for altoist Jimmy Jeter and tenorist Charles Pillars, and was the house band at the Plantation with several broadcasts a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well listen, tell me a little bit about that band. I've always heard of that band. But tell me about that band. I mean why is it called Jeter-Pillar's, and why --
Well, one -- it was two saxophone players, and one -- the alto player, now his name is Jimmy Jeter.
Yeah.
And the tenor player's name is Charles Pillars.
I see.
And one was an alto player and one was a tenor player.
One was a tenor saxophone player.
So they formed this band together and they called it Jeter Jetter Pillars.
Well, that band had been playing around for quite a little while, hadn't it?
Oh, it was a fantastic band. They used to do -- oh, we had at least four or five broadcasts a week out of the Plantation.
Oh, really?
Oh, yeah.
Really.
That was a fantastic band.
Well, who else was in that band?
Let's see if I can remember now.
Was that band -- had that band been going about four or five years when you joined it?
Yeah, they had been in -- well, this Italian fellow, his name was Tony --
That had the place?
Yeah, he owned the place. And well, they had kept Piller's band there for -- they were the house band, as a matter of fact.
Yeah, I see. Yeah.
And they were doing these broadcasts.
